brief.outcome: Grow the cooking channel for busy parents from about 2,050 subscribers toward 10,000 within a year, with honest titles and thumbnails, by finding and fixing what keeps new viewers from clicking, watching and subscribing.
brief.deliverable: A 12-week plan applied one approved change at a time: a diagnosis of the channel's click, watch and return problems, titles, thumbnail briefs and opening lines for the next videos, a series and weekly calendar sized to one video a week, and a monthly readout against the subscriber goal.

Titles, thumbnails and opening lines made, checked for honesty and approved by the owner before use
Each change registered as an experiment before it goes live, then read back with a verdict
Learnings and the next round saved in this project

research.approach: Practitioners treat a stalled small channel as a funnel with five links: discovery, click, watch, return and subscribe. They read the numbers per video, not as channel averages, find which link is weakest, and fix one link at a time. Packaging (title and thumbnail) and the opening of the video are tested before anything else, because they decide clicks and early drop-off. YouTube's own Test and Compare can run up to three titles or thumbnails per video and picks the winner by watch time. Topics are chosen from what people search for and from the channel's own best videos, and are packaged as a repeating series so viewers have a reason to come back and subscribe. Everything is judged on enough videos, not one.

sources.title: YouTube Help: A/B test titles and thumbnails
sources.note: Up to three variants per video, winner picked by watch time, finishes within about two weeks, desktop Studio only, labels Winner, Performed Same or Inconclusive. Page is undated; read 2026-11.

sources.title: YouTube Help: Measure key moments for audience retention
sources.note: How to read the retention curve and the share still watching at 30 seconds; needs 100 views. Page is undated; read 2026-11.

sources.title: The 1,000 Subscriber Wall: Why Channels Stall (PC Tech Magazine)

sources.title: YouTube Growth Strategy for Small Channels (OutlierKit)

steps.name: Pull per-video Studio numbers and check them
steps.why: Averages hide the few videos that work; the owner's figures are reports until checked.

steps.name: Study what works for channels of a similar size
steps.why: Outliers among comparable channels show topics and packaging that the audience already rewards.

steps.name: Find the weakest link: click, watch, return or subscribe
steps.why: Each link needs a different fix, and a 3.1% click rate with about a fifth of the video watched points two ways.

steps.name: Rank the fixes and let the owner choose
steps.why: One link at a time keeps results readable and fits one video a week.

steps.name: Make honest titles, thumbnails and opening lines before filming
steps.why: Packaging and the first 30 seconds set clicks and early drop-off.

steps.name: Turn proven topics into a repeating series and weekly calendar
steps.why: Series give viewers a reason to return and subscribe.

steps.name: Run changes as registered tests, one change at a time
steps.why: Test and Compare reads watch time on real viewers; a result is only trusted on enough videos.

pitfalls.text: Judging a change from one video; views swing by topic and by age of the video.
Chasing click rate alone with misleading packaging, which raises early drop-off and breaks the owner's honesty rule.
Changing a title or thumbnail while a test is running, which stops it.
Copying large channels whose reach comes from trust a small channel does not have.
Counting subscribers from views that never return, or from sub-for-sub tricks.

plan.name: Unstick the cooking channel and grow subscribers honestly

capabilities.why: Open Analytics, Reach and Audience retention and export per-video tables.

capabilities.name: Read public YouTube channels and search
capabilities.why: Look at similar channels' uploads, titles and view counts, and what viewers search for.

capabilities.name: Change titles and thumbnails in YouTube Studio (browser)

stages.name: Pin down the goal and the numbers
stages.goal: Turn the owner's words into a measured problem, a target, limits and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Pull the channel's per-video numbers
stages.goal: Export the Studio table and retention screenshots into the project data folder and note exactly what was pulled.

checks.name: Covers all 85 videos or states which are missing
Views and subscribers in the table add up to the Studio channel totals for the same dates
Each video has its age, so new videos are not compared with old ones

stages.name: Study comparable channels and search demand
stages.goal: Find home-cooking channels for busy parents near this size, list their outlier videos, and list what viewers search for.

checks.name: Peer channels are within about ten times this channel's size, or the gap is stated
An outlier is a video that beats its own channel's typical views, with the numbers shown
Every figure has the date it was read

stages.name: Check the numbers can be trusted
stages.goal: Check the owner's reported figures against the export, and flag videos too new or too small to judge.

checks.name: Average views, click-through rate and view duration are recomputed and compared with the owner's reported 900, 3.1% and 2:40
Channel click-through rate is weighted by impressions, not an average of averages
Videos under 100 views or under 28 days old are marked low-confidence
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and what that means for diagnosis

stages.name: Find the weakest link
stages.goal: Test the hypotheses against the per-video data and retention curves. Keep competing explanations.

checks.name: Every hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN, with the numbers behind it
Findings built on small or very new videos are marked low-confidence
Each main finding names a competing explanation
The finding says which link is weakest: discovery, click, watch, return or subscribe

stages.name: Rank what to try
stages.goal: Turn supported findings into a short list of ranked changes, each with the finding it rests on, the expected effect, effort, confidence, risk and how it will be measured. State plainly how far each is likely to move the 10,000 goal.

checks.name: Every option cites the finding it rests on
Every option has expected direction, effort, confidence, risk and how it will be measured
Options change one link at a time and fit one video a week
No option relies on misleading packaging
The gap between the reachable subscribers and 10,000 is stated, not hidden

stages.name: Owner chooses
stages.goal: The owner picks which changes to try first. Ask why when a top option is passed over, and record it.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over options and the reasons are recorded
Only chosen options are carried into production

stages.name: Write honest packaging and plan the series
stages.goal: For the next videos, write three title options, thumbnail briefs and the first 30 seconds word for word, each promise one the video keeps. Turn the proven topics and search demand into one or two named series and a 12-week calendar of one video a week. The owner reviews the packaging and the calendar together.

checks.name: Each title and thumbnail promise is delivered in the video, with the minute where it is delivered
Variants differ in one thing so a result can be read
No false claims, fake reactions or misleading images
Fits the busy-parent audience and the owner's own wording
Each slot traces to a proven topic or a search the audience makes
Exactly one video a week that the owner can film alone
Each video names what brings the viewer back for the next one

stages.optional_when: No packaging or opening change was chosen.

stages.name: Apply one approved change at a time
stages.goal: Register each test, then with the owner's approval apply a title or thumbnail test to one video in Studio and read the change back.

checks.name: Each test is written down with its expected result before it starts
Test and Compare availability for this channel and video is confirmed, or the change is made without it and marked untested
The title and thumbnail shown in Studio match what the owner approved
Nothing is changed while a test is running

stages.name: Read the results honestly
stages.goal: Read each test and the subscriber count against the registered expectation and the guardrails.

checks.name: A verdict is given only after the test window and enough videos; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE
Videos are compared at the same age and against the prior videos
Average view duration, views and weekly publishing are checked
The monthly subscriber count is shown against the 10,000 line

stages.name: Keep what we learned
stages.goal: Close each test, record wins and losses, propose rules with their scope, and plan the next round.

checks.name: Every test is closed with a verdict
Each rule says if it holds for this video, this channel or all channels

hypotheses.statement: Packaging is the weakest link: titles and thumbnails do not earn clicks from people who see them.
hypotheses.test: Impressions click-through rate per video, weighted by impressions, against the channel's own best videos and the traffic source.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Click-through rate is low on most videos and high only on a few distinct packaging styles.
hypotheses.refute_if: Click-through rate is steady and the best videos win on topic, not packaging.

hypotheses.statement: Viewers leave in the opening, so the video is not recommended further.
hypotheses.test: Retention at 30 seconds and the shape of the curve on the best and weakest videos.
hypotheses.confirm_if: A steep early drop on most videos, with a flatter curve on the best.
hypotheses.refute_if: Early retention is healthy and the loss comes later in the 12 minutes.

hypotheses.statement: Twelve-minute videos lose viewers because they run longer than the promise needs.
hypotheses.test: Average percentage viewed by video length, with the same topic compared where possible.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Shorter videos hold a clearly higher share of the video.
hypotheses.refute_if: Share watched does not vary with length.

hypotheses.statement: Topics do not match what busy parents search for or what this audience rewards.
hypotheses.test: Views per topic, search versus browse traffic, and peer outliers on the same topics.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Few videos get search traffic and peer outliers cluster on topics the channel has not covered.
hypotheses.refute_if: Search traffic is healthy and topics match the peer outliers.

hypotheses.statement: Viewers watch once and do not come back or subscribe, because nothing links one video to the next.
hypotheses.test: Returning viewers and subscribers gained per 1,000 views, by video.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Subscribers per 1,000 views is low even on well-watched videos, and returning viewers are few.
hypotheses.refute_if: Well-watched videos convert at a healthy rate and the problem is reach.

hypotheses.statement: The reported figures are not what Studio shows for the whole period.
hypotheses.test: Recompute average views, click-through rate and view duration from the export.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Recomputed figures differ from the reported ones by more than a few percent.

measurement.window: Each Test and Compare run for up to the platform's two-week limit, then judge the change over at least the next 5 videos compared with the 10 before, at the same video age. Subscribers are read every month.
measurement.min_volume: No verdict on a packaging change from fewer than 5 videos or from a test Studio labels Inconclusive; retention findings need at least 100 views per video.
measurement.stop_rule: Stop and review if average view duration or views per video fall on the changed videos, or if any title or thumbnail is found to over-promise. Otherwise finish the window before judging.
